title: Outlook for Compliance Officers on Mac: Labels, Policy Tips and Templates for 2026

intro: Outlook for compliance officers on Mac is the new Outlook client, and it handles the core review tools: sensitivity labels, retention labels, policy tips and templates. Some of those tools stay off until your admin turns them on, and a few features are missing, so check before you rely on them. This guide shows what to test, how to use templates safely, and where Lazur helps.
tldr: Check your Outlook version first. Microsoft's page said support for legacy Outlook for Mac would end in October 2026.
Data loss prevention (DLP) policy tips are off by default on Mac. Ask IT whether your admin turned them on.
Built-in templates work through File > Save As Template. The My Templates add-in does not work in shared mailboxes opened in Mac Outlook.
Test search and rules before you rely on them for a legal hold or a review.
Lazur points, explains, drafts and dictates. It does not click, file or send anything for you.

blocks.text: No study we found measures how compliance officers use Outlook for Mac. The guidance here comes from the features Microsoft documents for compliance work: labels, data loss prevention (DLP) policy tips, templates, and the release notes that change them. Treat this page as a checklist. Then confirm each item with your IT team, because your organization sets the rules.
Check your Outlook version before you start

Outlook for Mac now runs as the new client. The latest build in Microsoft's release notes is 16.114.3, released October 27, 2026. Microsoft's support page says support for legacy Outlook for Mac will end in October 2026. That month has passed. Check which client you run today, and plan your work around the new one.

To check your build, choose Outlook > About Outlook and write down the number. If you need to go back, use Help > Revert to Legacy Outlook. Support depends on your Microsoft 365, Office or Outlook license, so confirm that before you count on the old client. Accounts added in one version are not added to the other automatically. You may need to set up each account twice.

items: Open Outlook and choose Outlook > About Outlook.
Write down the version and build numbers.
Compare the build with the latest one in Microsoft's Office for Mac release notes.
If your build is behind, update Office before you test rules, search or templates.

blocks.title: Test before you trust the switch
blocks.text: Users in a Microsoft Q&A thread report that search, rules and junk mail handling broke after the forced switch. One user says emails more than two years old came back after a migration. No Microsoft staff replied in that thread. Treat these reports as anecdotes, then test your own setup.
Sensitivity and retention labels on Mac

The Mac client supports sensitivity labels and retention labels. A sensitivity label marks what a message contains, such as confidential client data. A retention label controls how long the item must be kept. Your organization defines the label choices, usually in Microsoft Purview, so the options you see come from your admin, not from Outlook itself.

Here is a worked example. You draft a message to an outside auditor that includes client account numbers. If your DLP policy covers account numbers, and your admin has turned on policy tips, a tip may appear before you send. Read the tip before you click past it. Then remove the account numbers, or send the file through the secure channel your policy names.

Retention and holds are different tools. A retention label sets how long content is kept. A legal hold is a separate control that stops deletion. Do not assume one replaces the other. If a matter needs preservation, confirm with IT which control applies and get that in writing before you change folders or labels.
Purview DLP policy tips: why you may not see them

Purview DLP policy tips for Outlook on macOS are off by default. An admin must turn on the setting named Enable Purview Data Loss Prevention (DLP) policy tips in Outlook, in the Microsoft 365 Apps admin center. The setting can target single users or groups, which helps with a pilot. If you never see a tip, that does not prove your mail is clean. It may only mean nobody turned the tips on.

rows: Off by default on macOS. An admin must enable them.
Ask IT whether tips are on for your account.
All sensitivity labels are supported in the policy tip reference.
Ask which labels apply to your team.
Documented for Android and iOS. The page does not say it works on Mac.
Do not assume it appears on your Mac.
Documented for Android and iOS. Not stated for Mac.
Do not rely on it as a Mac safeguard.

blocks.text: Read each tip before you decide. Microsoft's reference says all trainable classifiers, custom sensitive information types and EDM types are supported for email. That means a tip can fire on a pattern you did not expect. Keep a short log of false alerts, with the message type and the pattern. Send that log to your admin, so they can tune the policy.
Templates for approved compliance language

Templates save you from rewriting the same disclaimer, request reply or closing notice. Outlook for Mac offers two methods. The built-in method saves a message with File > Save As Template. You reuse it from File > New > Mail From Template. It needs a Microsoft 365 subscription and Outlook for Mac version 15.35 (170610) or later.

rows: Microsoft 365 subscription and Outlook for Mac 15.35 (170610) or later
Microsoft's article does not say whether it works in shared mailboxes.
A Microsoft Exchange account. Open it from the New Mail ribbon, then the +Template button.
Not available in shared mailboxes opened in Mac Outlook. An admin can turn it off.
blocks.caption: Two template methods in Outlook for Mac, based on Microsoft's template article.

blocks.text: Here is a worked example. You keep a reply for data access requests. Write it once, with placeholders in square brackets for the request date and the reference number. Choose File > Save As Template and name it clearly, such as Access Reply 2026. Each time, open File > New > Mail From Template, fill the brackets and check the content before you send.

Templates go stale. A saved reply that cites an old policy number can cause real trouble. When you save a template, put a review date in your calendar. See /how-to/create-a-calendar-event-in-outlook for the steps. Keep one owner for each template, so edits do not drift across the team.
Shared compliance mailboxes on Mac

Many compliance teams work from a shared inbox, such as a complaints or privacy address. Mac Outlook has two problems with that setup. The My Templates add-in does not work in shared mailboxes opened in Mac Outlook. Microsoft also lists Send as and Send on behalf of an Office 365 Group as not supported. If your shared address is a group, you cannot send as it from the Mac client.

Set up the mailbox first. The steps are on /how-to/add-a-shared-mailbox-in-outlook. Then send one test message from the shared address to a colleague. If the send fails, ask IT which route they support. Do not improvise with a personal account, because that can leave a record outside the team.
Search, rules and folders: run your own tests

Search and rules fail quietly. The Q&A thread reports search and rule problems after the switch. A failed search during a review looks like an empty result. Run a short check before you rely on either one. Use a message you already know is in your archive, and confirm each result by eye.

items: Pick a message you know is in your archive. Search for a word from its subject.
If it does not come back, search by sender and by date range, then compare.
Create a test rule that moves one message from a test sender to a test folder. Send that message to confirm the rule fires.
Mark one known message as junk. Confirm it leaves the inbox and stays out of the inbox after a new sync.
Write down what worked and what did not, with your build number, and send the note to IT.

blocks.text: For filter steps, read /how-to/search-with-filters-in-outlook. For rule steps, read /how-to/create-a-rule-in-outlook. Those pages cover the clicks. This section covers the tests you run before you trust the result.
Known gaps and fixes that affect review work

Microsoft lists two gaps that matter for reviews. Notes and Tasks views are not natively available in the new client. If your reviewers track findings in Tasks, move that list before you switch, or keep the legacy client for those users. Send as and Send on behalf of Office 365 Groups are not supported, as covered above.

Recent release notes list fixes that matter to compliance. Version 16.114, released October 14, 2026, kept folder archive policies saved after folder sync. The same build made DLP alerts and policy tips show their full text. Those items were fixed in that build, so earlier builds had them. Check your build against the notes before you trust a tip.
Where Lazur fits in your Outlook day

Lazur is a voice assistant for the Mac that lives in the notch. Hold ⌥ ⌘ to ask about anything on your screen, and Lazur answers out loud. Ask where a control sits, and Lazur draws a circle and a label around it. Ask how to do something, and Lazur guides you one click at a time, waiting for each click.

Lazur does not click buttons, edit files or operate other apps for you. You do the clicks. It is not a plugin or add-in for Outlook or any other app, and it has no partnership with any app maker. That matters for audit trails. Every send, label and template change still happens under your own login.
Privacy checks before you ask about a message

Lazur listens and looks at the screen only while you hold the shortcut. Audio and the screenshot go to AI providers so they can answer you. They are not stored, and content is never used to train AI models. Those are the product facts. Your company's rules still apply. Many compliance teams limit which AI tools can see client data, so check that policy first.

blocks.title: Check policy before a live matter
blocks.text: Before you ask about a live matter, check whether your policy allows AI tools near that content. If it does not, ask Lazur only about menu locations and settings, not about the message itself.
Dictation for review notes

Hold fn to dictate clean, formatted text at the cursor in any app. Dictation is useful for file notes, which you write often and read rarely. Lazur also keeps snippets, a personal dictionary and clipboard slots. Add your team's names, policy numbers and internal terms to the dictionary, so the text comes out right.

Here is a file note you might dictate after a review. Reviewed the refund thread. No policy breach found. One customer detail in the body needs redaction before any external share. Escalated to legal. Read the note back before you save it, because dictation can mishear names and numbers.

blocks.title: Check the window first
blocks.text: Dictated text goes wherever your cursor sits. Check the window before you speak, especially in a shared mailbox or an open case file.
Triage for large threads and fast skims

Microsoft's WorkLab 2025 report says the average worker receives 117 emails a day, and most are skimmed in under 60 seconds. It also reports that emails with 20 or more recipients rose 7% over the past year. The survey covered about 31,000 knowledge workers in 31 markets. Those numbers describe all knowledge workers, so use them as a rough guide only.

Large threads are where mistakes happen. A reply-all to 20 people can send a customer's personal data to people who should not see it. Use Delay delivery to catch that. The steps are on /how-to/delay-delivery-of-an-email-in-outlook. Turn it on before you need it, not during a bad afternoon.

Use folders and pins for the threads you must return to. Create one folder for each open review. The steps are on /how-to/create-a-folder-in-outlook. Pin the active message as well, using the steps on /how-to/pin-an-email-in-outlook. Then your open items stay visible while the rest of the inbox moves.
Mistakes compliance officers make in Outlook for Mac

items: Assuming DLP policy tips are on. Ask IT to confirm for your account.
Saving a template in a shared mailbox and expecting it to appear for the whole team.
Trusting search for a legal hold before you have tested it on known messages.
Sending as a group address that Mac Outlook does not support.
Running the legacy and new clients on the same account, then losing track of which one holds the latest mail.
Pasting confidential text into an AI tool without checking your company's policy.

blocks.text: Each mistake costs more than it looks. The fix is usually a short check, not a new tool. Most of these checks take a few minutes and one note to IT. Write the note with your build number, so the team can reproduce the problem.
What to do next

Start with the version check. Then ask IT two questions: whether DLP policy tips are enabled for your account, and whether the My Templates add-in is allowed. Run the search and rule tests on a quiet afternoon. Save one template for the reply you send most. Then try Lazur on a message that holds no confidential content.
When you are ready, compare plans on /pricing or get the app at /download. Lazur runs only on macOS for now, on Apple silicon and Intel Macs. Windows is planned, not available.

faq.question: Which version of Outlook for Mac should a compliance officer use?
faq.answer: Use the new Outlook client, which Microsoft is moving everyone to. The latest build in Microsoft's release notes is 16.114.3, released October 27, 2026. Microsoft's support page said legacy support would end in October 2026, and that month has passed. Check your build, then test search and rules before you rely on them.

faq.question: Why don't I see DLP policy tips in Outlook for Mac?
faq.answer: Purview DLP policy tips for Outlook on macOS are off by default. An admin must turn on the setting in the Microsoft 365 Apps admin center. Ask IT whether the tips are enabled for your account. A missing tip does not prove that a message is clean.

faq.question: Can I use My Templates in a shared mailbox on Mac?
faq.answer: No. Microsoft says the My Templates add-in is not available in shared mailboxes opened in Mac Outlook. The built-in template controls are a separate method. Microsoft's article does not say whether they work in shared mailboxes, so test them before the team depends on them.

faq.question: Does Lazur read my email or send it to a server?
faq.answer: Lazur listens and looks at the screen only while you hold the shortcut. Audio and the screenshot go to AI providers so they can answer you. They are not stored, and content is never used to train AI models. Your company's policy on AI tools still applies, so check it before you use Lazur near confidential content.

faq.question: Can Lazur file emails, set rules or send messages for me?
faq.answer: No. Lazur points, explains, answers out loud, drafts and types text. It does not click buttons or operate other apps for you. You do the clicks, and Lazur guides you one click at a time when you ask how to do something.

faq.question: Is Lazur an add-in for Outlook?
faq.answer: No. Lazur is a voice assistant for the Mac. It is not a plugin or add-in for Outlook or any other app. It has no partnership with any app maker. It runs on macOS, and Windows is planned, not available.

faq.question: Does Outlook for Mac support sensitivity labels?
faq.answer: Microsoft's release notes and support pages say the Mac client supports sensitivity and retention labels. The labels you can apply come from your organization's setup. Ask your admin which labels apply to your team before you start a review.
